chunk_findings.detail: Both scenarios now flip `schedule.phase_full_suite` to `off` immediately before completing `P1`, and never restore it. The reported symptom — "`ddflow_complete id=P1` refused because the full suite has not passed on P1's merged tree" — is a property of the scenario itself (it never runs `ddflow ci run --full`), and the change does not remove that property; it removes the check that surfaced it. Concrete consequence: a regression in the enforcement of the default (`require`) close gate is now undetectable end-to-end. Delete the `schedule.phase_full_suite == "require"` branch in the completion path (or make it a no-op) and both scenarios still pass, because they set the setting to `off` two lines earlier — before this diff they would have gone red, and per the task description they *are* the end-to-end scenarios for this flow. The setting also persists for the remainder of each scenario, so every later "phase completes" assertion in these files is validated under a configuration the product does not ship by default. If the scenario genuinely must not run the suite, the check should be scoped to that one completion (and the default-path coverage kept in a scenario that leaves the setting alone) rather than muting the gate for the rest of the run.

chunk_findings.detail: Setting `schedule.phase_full_suite` to `off` immediately before `ddflow_complete(id="P1")` makes the scenario pass by removing the gate under test, not by satisfying it. Concretely: with the fixed tree, if a regression makes the full suite fail on P1's merged tree (or if the suite is never run at all), the pre-change scenario fails at `alpha.tool("ddflow_complete", id="P1", ...)` with "complete P1 refused", whereas post-change it reports `code == 0` and the check `"P1 closes"` / `"phase P1 completes once every task is done"` passes, because the configure call in the same scope has disabled the default `require` gate. The scenario therefore no longer detects the exact condition the bug B7f54dbf1e3 was filed against, and the bug's acceptance criterion (full test suite passing on P1's merged tree) is left unaddressed.

chunk_findings.detail: The line it replaces acted on the demo workspace that owns P1 (`alpha.tool("ddflow_configure", set="schedule.phase_full_suite", value="off")`), whereas the replacement goes through the scenario-harness helper `sc.ddflow(...)`, so the full-suite run is not scoped to the `alpha` repo whose `schedule.phase_full_suite` (default `require`) gates the following `alpha.tool("ddflow_complete", id="P1", ...)`. The author's own triage for this item confirms the consequence: "ci run --full does not record in demo repo (DX-ci-full-mcp-and-scenario)". Given that, running `ddflow ci run --full --command "python3 -m pytest tests/ -q"` before the close cannot write the full-suite pass that the P1 gate reads (the demo workspace tree, and possibly a `tests/` path that does not exist there, so pytest exits 4 and nothing is recorded), so `ddflow_complete(id="P1")` still encounters the same unmet gate as before the change and `sc.check("P1 closes", code == 0, text)` remains red. If the scenario nonetheless reports `code == 0`, the close is passing for a reason other than the gate being satisfied, in which case the new comment ("record a full-suite pass on the merged tree so the default close check stays exercised end to end") is false and the `phase_full_suite` default is not exercised at all — the same defect the superseded HIGH finding described, merely relocated from "switch the gate off" to "run something that is not recorded for that repo".

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed finding stands and the triage does not answer it: the change still edits the two demo modules that are far over the 20 KB limit in D-small-files (~840 and ~650 lines, with long single-line `sc.check` message strings) instead of splitting them into a package of smaller modules, and it grows them further. "Accepted trade-off", "demo file size pre-existing" and the note that the close path has other coverage are not a fix and not a probe of the file-size rule, which is a recorded project decision that applies to this change; the added `ddflow ci run --full ...` invocation plus its two-line comment in `scenario_mcp_orchestration.py` and `scenario_full_lifecycle.py` is exactly the kind of context growth the decision asks to avoid by modularising.

chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` decides baseline-red with `red = outcome == "failed" and all(i in failing for i in ids)`. `all()` over an empty sequence is vacuously `True`, so when `ids == []` the function reports `{"red": True, ...}` as soon as the base run's outcome is `"failed"` — which is precisely the situation this feature exists to handle (main is red). `candidate_ids` itself returns `[]` in exactly the cases the module docstring says must stay FAILED ("any id the output did not name (a capped list, a fail-fast run)" — it returns `[]` when `fail_fast` or `ev["failed_tests_more"]` is set, and for any gate outside `GATES`). So the natural call sequence — `ids = candidate_ids(gate, command, ev, fail_fast)`, `res = on_base(repo, base, gdef, ids, run)`, record `partial` when `res["red"]` — takes a fail-fast or truncated `ci`/`unit_tests` failure on an already-red main, runs the whole gate in the base scratch tree (the base run fails, `outcome == "failed"`), and records `baseline-red: , bug B...` with an empty id list. The gate is then `partial` with a coverage gap over zero ids, so `complete` is unblocked with no failing test actually tied to the base, contradicting the stated contract that these inputs leave the gate FAILED. The guard needs to require a non-empty `ids` (e.g. `ids and outcome == "failed" and all(...)`), or `candidate_ids` returning `[]` must be rejected before `on_base` is invoked.

chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` re-runs the failing ids in a *fresh* checkout of the base (`W.scratch_tree(repo, sha, ...)`, then `run(replace(gdef, command=cmd), tree.path)`), but it carries over nothing of the process state the branch's gate run depended on. The whole point of the comparison is "main fails the same way", yet the scratch worktree only reproduces main's *tracked source*; the installed/editable package, `.venv`/`node_modules`, built extensions and gitignored fixtures all live in the branch's checkout and are neither present in nor redirected to the new worktree. Concrete case: a repo whose CI/dev gate is `pip install -e .` + `pytest`. On the branch, test `t1` fails because of the change. `candidate_ids` returns `["t1"]`, a scratch tree of main is made and `pytest t1` is executed there — but `import <pkg>` still resolves through the editable `.pth` to the *branch's* source path, so main's checkout is never actually exercised and `t1` fails again for the branch's reason. `outcome == "failed"` and `"t1" in failing`, so `red=True`, the gate is recorded `partial`, and `complete` accepts a genuinely branch-caused regression as baseline-red. The same happens without editable installs whenever the failing test needs a gitignored file that is present in the working tree but absent from a fresh `git worktree add` (fixture data, `node_modules`, compiled artifacts): the id fails in the scratch tree for an environment reason and is mis-attributed to main.
